headline: Highest risk is capability conflict from Aider’s shared git writes; prompt injection, leakage, and compliance risks are otherwise low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and uses stdin/stdout, so manual copy-paste or file-based instruction smuggling is plausible. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable, so it is not an active injector. The pathway exists but is limited to unusual bridging by the operator.
conditions: IF the operator copies B’s text into Aider prompts or repo files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is converted into a writable or interactive agent, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep B read-only and documentation-only.
Do not paste B output into Aider prompts without review.
Use a separate scratch file for any copied text.
Add a prompt delimiter convention for pasted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, network, or API surfaces. There is no shared workspace or authenticated data path shown, so leakage from B into A is not evidenced; the main risk is operator-mediated copying of code or notes.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive material from B into Aider’s repo or prompt, Aider may transmit it to a model provider.
IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in the shared repo.
Use a redacted scratch workspace for copied content.
Restrict Aider to non-sensitive branches.
Review outbound prompts before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state is via a shared git repo. python-cheatsheet cannot write, so it does not add conflict, but Aider alone can still race with other instances or external git actors. Because the shared mutable repo is explicit, the default is dangerous for concurrent edits.
conditions: IF another process edits the same git repo while Aider runs, conflicts can occur.
IF multiple Aider instances target the same repo, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Run only one writer per repo at a time.
Use separate branches for each task.
Pull and rebase before each edit cycle.
Pause other git automation during Aider sessions.
requires-engineering: add repo locking or transactional merge coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and commits, while python-cheatsheet is a reference document that may be treated as authoritative input if copied into Aider. The pair does not show autonomous downstream actions, but Aider can act on unverified content from B, creating a default-path error cascade when the operator uses B as source material.
conditions: IF B text is copied into Aider as authoritative guidance, Aider may implement incorrect changes.
IF Aider commits changes based on unverified reference snippets, errors can propagate into git history.
mitigations: Verify B-derived claims before editing code.
Use tests after each Aider commit.
Limit B to reference lookup, not source of truth.
Review diffs before accepting commits.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class or residency mismatch is evidenced. Aider touches source code and git history, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes. Without PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy differences in the profiles, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF PHI, regulated PII, or secrets are introduced into the shared workflow, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF either profile is updated with residency or retention constraints, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data-class boundaries for the repo.
Review retention settings for any logs.
Use a non-sensitive test repository.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
